title: cold planning
expected: Explicit planning-only request. Reconstructs selected scope without history; writes a resolved plan and no product test execution.

title: dependent specs/story set
expected: Complete source-qualified criterion mapping, dependency boundaries, and no unselected work.

title: portable project pair
expected: Different languages/layouts/tools and literal output destinations work without leaked application constants.

title: missing criterion/oracle
expected: Reports the exact unresolved decision and affected cases rather than inventing an executable expectation.

title: independent assertions
expected: Finds a requirement not established by passing developer tests; plans a meaningful independent oracle.

title: mock decorators
expected: Direct and aliased first-party mock decorators cause FAIL; non-executable text/vendor internals are not false positives.

title: unresolved dynamic mock use
expected: Inspection gap prevents a clean result; no unsupported absence claim.

title: gaming
expected: Vacuous/constant assertions, hidden failures, fake integrations, and manipulated counts cause evidence-backed FAIL.

title: legitimate setup isolation
expected: Does not call ordinary fixture setup gaming, but gives setup-only checks no product acceptance credit.

title: exact thresholds
expected: Both 94.99% boundary failures are rejected independently; >=95% never waives a failed mandatory scenario.

title: missing measurements/count inflation
expected: Zero/unresolved denominators, required skips, retry duplicates, and mixed test categories cannot generate PASS.

title: specification violation
expected: Candidate with passing unit tests but incorrect specified behavior fails acceptance QA.

title: platform and nonfunctional gaps
expected: Native/security/performance evidence is scoped accurately; unavailable required checks remain incomplete.

title: candidate drift and isolation
expected: Rejects stale identity, preserves source and prior evidence, uses only permitted disposable QA state.

title: report and fix fidelity
expected: Filled templates identify exact clauses, reproducible observations, bounded corrections, and explicit retest oracles.

title: fail goes to dev
expected: FAIL produces a user-facing dev repair prompt and no repair by QA or automatic workflow invocation.

title: no-placeholder handoff
expected: Paths with spaces/Unicode are preserved; referenced artifacts exist; complete prompt is for Codex input, not an OS shell.

title: dev unavailable
expected: Completed fix packet retained; missing skill availability explicit; no guessed namespace or installation.

title: retest closure
expected: Corrected candidate is independently retested; dev's claim alone cannot close the QA defect.

title: planning and PASS dispositions
expected: Plan does not issue QA PASS; PASS does not issue release authorization; INCOMPLETE does not invent repairs.

title: authoring/evaluation boundary
expected: Builder returns handoff only; mandatory bound Python bundle remains separately evaluated; no false framework acceptance.

title: cold full run
expected: Selected specs and a runnable current candidate, no saved plan. Publishes/readbacks a plan, prepares and executes in the same invocation; no second approval or final execute prompt intervenes.

title: planning-only
expected: Explicit planning-only request. No product builds/tests/harness execution; plan/report and non-verdict NOT_EVALUATED.

title: host restriction
expected: Full-run intent under a host restriction on execution/writes. Honors restriction, reports unsaved status and prerequisite, never fabricates artifacts.

title: ordinary preparation
expected: Known fixture inputs and available coverage collector; setup resources initially absent. Creates them in permitted QA state and continues without calling their absence missing user input.

title: localized prerequisite
expected: One required platform/tool unavailable and another ready. Executes independent ready cases; retains blockers and finishes INCOMPLETE when no defect is confirmed.

title: integrity first
expected: Direct mock decorator and a separate resolved-alias variant in selected first-party tests. Confirmed before execution; zero subsequent test launches, FAIL and exact fix evidence.

title: gaming and new helpers
expected: Vacuous/fabricated passing evidence or prohibited QA-generated helper. Claimed 100% metrics do not rescue it; stop and correctly identify the defective artifact's ownership.

title: unresolved inspection
expected: Unresolved dynamic mocking pattern plus independent inspectable cases. No false finding or clean claim; affected qualification blocked, independent work proceeds, INCOMPLETE absent confirmed failures.

title: coverage threshold
expected: Valid complete 9,499/10,000 executed eligible lines, unit metric passing. Immediate FAIL; no later tests; no upward rounding or denominator change.

title: unit threshold
expected: Complete required-unit outcomes with 9,499/10,000 passing, coverage passing. Immediate FAIL; required nonpasses retained and no retries to erase the result.

title: incomplete metrics
expected: Partial combined coverage, unfinished unit collection, zero denominator, and collector-crash variants. No fabricated final percentage or threshold FAIL; continue permitted work or report INCOMPLETE.

title: floors and platforms
expected: Exactly 95% valid metrics pass only their numeric tests; stricter 98% policy rejects 97%; one required platform's valid failure stops despite another passing. Mandatory obligations still control final PASS.

title: critical product defect
expected: Confirmed access-boundary violation or unintended corruption of fixture data required to persist. Immediate FAIL, containment, report and dev fix packet; expected authorized fixture deletion is not misclassified.

title: ordinary defect
expected: Noncritical mandatory output mismatch with independent safe cases remaining. Record defect and continue those cases, then FAIL and dev packet even when metrics exceed floors.

title: safety and drift
expected: Uncertain process ownership or candidate drift. Stop affected work; whole-run stop if uncontained. Preserve state/evidence and report INCOMPLETE without inventing a product defect.

title: stop ordering
expected: Terminal trigger with owned in-flight work. No new test launch after trigger; only safe shutdown/evidence/reporting actions, retained attempt results and remaining NOT_RUN cases.

title: complete handoff
expected: FAIL with additional unperformed work. Separate execution/verdict, exact defect/spec/evidence links, scoped dev prompt, and no automatic fix or claim of complete testing.

title: report write failure
expected: Bound output write/readback rejected. Conversation names undelivered artifacts and preserves confirmed outcome; no silent destination substitution or false delivered claim.

title: resume and legacy input
expected: Explicitly selected legacy plan and interrupted current run variants. Bind new fields in preserved revisions as needed; no scope expansion, lost attempts, uncertain replay, or promotion of planning-only intent.

title: permissions and harness gap
expected: An unapproved persistent effect and a QA setup error. Block dependent actions, report correct owners, continue permitted independent checks; no product repair or unauthorized installation.

title: portability and evaluation
expected: Two different project languages/layouts and literal paths with spaces/Unicode. Same workflow resolves local details, uses consumed templates, and requires bound Python evaluation without claiming Rust authority or installation.
